# [TASK] Add audit-check.py to verify the mechanical parts of the standard

## Task
Add `infrastructure/scripts/audit-check.py`, which checks issues against the
mechanical parts of the backlog standard.

The standard in `AGENTS.md` and `.claude/skills/audit-artifacts/` is mostly
prose a person has to judge. These parts are not, so re-reading them by hand
on every audit wastes the auditor's attention and misses things:

- exactly one type label, exactly one priority label, an assignee
- no retired `sprint-N` label
- no section holding a second copy of a GitHub field: `## Child Stories`,
  `## Technical Tasks`, `## Sprint`, or a `Parent: #N` line
- a parent link, or a `## No parent` section stating why not
- the template's sections all present
- no acceptance criterion closing on a date instead of a proof
- a Bug whose priority label disagrees with its body
- no closed issue with an unchecked criterion or an open child

It found 24 problems across #251's own subtree on its first run, including
#255 closed with all 6 criteria unchecked.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] `audit-check.py <n> --tree` reports problems for an issue and
      everything under it, `--all` for the board, `--quiet` for counts
      (`test_audit_check.py ExitCodeTest`)
- [x] It exits non-zero when it finds a problem and zero when clean, so it
      can gate a run
      (`test_audit_check.py ExitCodeTest.test_a_problem_exits_non_zero`)
- [x] Every check maps to a rule stated in `AGENTS.md` or the skill, with
      no rule invented in the script. Each test names the rule it covers
      (`python3 -m unittest discover -s infrastructure/scripts -p 'test_*.py'`)
- [x] The docstring states what it cannot check: whether a claim is true,
      whether a named test proves anything, and whether the prose reads well
      (`head -20 infrastructure/scripts/audit-check.py`)
- [x] Running it on #251 --tree reports 0 problems
      (`audit-check.py 251 --tree`)

## Estimate
**Hours:** 3

## Notes
An audit issue's criteria are inspection statements with no code behind
them, so before this script they could only be confirmed by re-reading. The
mechanical half is now a command.

The script's own criteria are proven by `test_audit_check.py`, which builds
synthetic issues in memory rather than calling GitHub, so the suite does not
go red when somebody fixes an issue on the real board. The original proof
for the exit-code criterion was `audit-check.py 252`, which stopped proving
anything when #252 was deleted: it returned 1 for "not found", not for a
rule violation.

`## Sprint` joined the banned-section check here, which is what makes #311's
fourth criterion continuously enforced instead of a one-off sweep.
